result.title: DIVE: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Interaction with Visual Engagement in Continuous Streams
result.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially improved spoken interaction and video understanding. Existing online and streaming benchmarks primarily assess causal multimodal perception through timestamped question answering, whereas real-world interaction requires models to continuously identify task-relevant multimodal cues and decide whether, when, and how to respond. This leaves open how well current models can sustain real-time interaction throughout an evolving multimodal stream. To address this gap, we introduce DIVE, a benchmark for evaluating full-duplex interaction with visual engagement under continuous and realistic multimodal streams. It organizes six tasks into three complementary interaction scenarios. (1) Proactive Intervention evaluates whether models can identify emerging visual or semantic cues and intervene at the appropriate moment. (2) Continuous Engagement evaluates sustained participation through continuous visual tracking and visually grounded query interaction. (3) Interaction Coordination evaluates how models coordinate listening and speaking under overlapping and multi-party interactions. DIVE contains 525 audio/video samples with fine-grained human annotations and precise temporal metadata. Its evaluation protocol separates response quality, participation decisions, and response timing. We evaluate representative real-time models using response quality, window response rates, and reaction latency. Experiments show that leading real-time models achieve sub-second average response latency, yet their average window response rates remain at or below 53.77%. Response quality varies substantially across models and tasks, with adapting ongoing responses to newly arriving information remaining particularly challenging. We hope DIVE facilitates progress toward more natural and capable real-time multimodal interactive systems.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DIVE 基准，在连续音视频流上评估 MLLM 的全双工交互与视觉参与，覆盖主动介入、持续跟踪及听说协调，并将响应质量、参与决策与时延分开评价。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「是否、何时、如何响应」的参与决策与持续视觉线索跟踪，和 LVR 的 STOP/LOOK 及证据筛选评价直接相关，可供核查其时序标注与窗口响应率指标能否迁移；但论文本身不研究 latent 推理状态。
